replays.title: Morphy at the opera
replays.story: Morphy was dragged to the opera and asked to play during the show. He wanted to watch the stage, so he finished the game in 17 moves. Every move makes a threat; the king never gets to castle.

10.prompt: Black just traded the bishop. Where does Morphy's bishop belong?
10.why: Bc4 points at f7, the square only the king guards, and threatens to take it with the queen. Development with a threat.

12.prompt: Make two threats with one move.
12.hint: The queen can hit two pawns at once.
12.why: Qb3 attacks f7 and b7 together. Black can only answer one, and must use the queen to defend, which blocks its own bishop.

16.hint: The knight on f6 guards the king. Tie it down.
16.why: Bg5 pins the knight to the queen. A pinned piece cannot defend anything else.

18.prompt: They attack your bishop with b5. Morphy does not retreat. What does he do?
18.hint: Give a piece to keep the king in the middle.
18.why: Nxb5! If they take, the b-file and the a4-e8 diagonal open onto a king that has not castled. Retreating would give Black time to castle. Tal would have played this too.

22.hint: Which way puts a rook on the open file?
22.why: O-O-O brings the rook to the d-file in one move, aimed at the pinned knight on d7. Castling is an attacking move here.

24.prompt: Remove the piece holding everything together.
24.hint: The pinned knight is the only defender. Count what happens after they recapture.
24.why: Rxd7! A rook for a knight, but the second rook comes to d1 and the pin is back with one defender fewer. Material is fuel.

26.hint: The rook you spent needs a replacement.
26.why: Rd1. Same file, same pin, same threats, and Black is a move slower.

30.prompt: The final trick. The knight on d7 is the last defender of d8.
30.hint: Pull it away. Give whatever it takes.
30.why: Qb8+! A deflection: the knight must take, and when it leaves d7 the d-file is open for Rd8 mate.

notes.6: Morphy opens the centre at once.
notes.8: The queen comes to f3 and already looks at f7.
notes.32: Checkmate. Morphy gave a knight, a rook and a queen, and every one of them bought a line or a tempo.

replays.finale: Seventeen moves. Black never castled because Morphy never gave him a free move.

replays.title: The Immortal Game
replays.story: A friendly game between rounds of a tournament. Anderssen gives a bishop, both rooks and the queen, and mates with the three small pieces he has left.

20.prompt: Black attacks your bishop with c6. Anderssen leaves it there. What does he play instead?
20.hint: Get a rook behind the g-pawn, so every pawn push hits the queen.
20.why: Rg1! The bishop is bait. The rook behind the g-pawn means g4-g5 will come with threats on the queen, and every one of those is a free move.

22.why: h4 attacks the queen. She must move again. Black's only developed piece is being kicked around while White brings everyone.

26.prompt: Bring the queen in with a threat.
26.hint: Threaten the f4 pawn and point at f7.
26.why: Qf3 threatens Bxf4 winning the queen's last square, and the queen eyes the kingside.

32.prompt: Bring the last piece in with a threat.
32.hint: The knight can jump to a square that threatens Nc7 with a fork.
32.why: Nd5 threatens Nc7+, forking king and rook. Now every White piece is in the attack.

34.prompt: Black took b2 and threatens both rooks. Anderssen's answer is the most famous move in chess.
34.hint: Let the rooks go. Block the queen's way back.
34.why: Bd6!! Both rooks hang, but the bishop shuts the black queen out of the defence and prepares Be7 mate. Material is fuel.

36.prompt: Black took the rook on g1. Keep the queen out.
36.hint: A pawn move that cuts the long diagonal.
36.why: e5! The queen on a1 cannot come back to defend g7 along the diagonal. The second rook is also left to be taken.

40.hint: A knight check that takes a pawn.
40.why: Nxg7+ drives the king to d8 and opens the way for the queen.

42.hint: Give the queen so the bishop can mate.
42.why: Qf6+! The knight must take, and Be7 is mate: the king on d8 is boxed in by its own pieces.

notes.24: Another push, another tempo on the queen.
notes.38: The king steps aside. Anderssen is now down a bishop and both rooks.
notes.44: Checkmate with a bishop and two knights.

replays.finale: Anderssen gave almost everything and kept the only thing that matters: the initiative.

replays.title: The Evergreen Game
replays.story: Anderssen gives pawns early to open roads, keeps Black's king in the middle, and finishes with a rook sacrifice, a queen sacrifice and a double check.

12.prompt: White is a pawn down and Black threatens to take another. Castle or save the pawn?
12.hint: Your king first; the pawns were spent on purpose.
12.why: O-O. The pawns bought open lines and time. Castling makes the king safe and brings the rook toward the centre.

14.prompt: Hit two things with the queen.
14.why: Qb3 eyes f7, guarded only by the king, and b7 behind it.

16.prompt: Attack the queen and open lines.
16.why: e5 kicks the queen and opens the long diagonal for the bishop that will come to a3.

18.prompt: Bring a rook to the king in the middle.
18.why: Re1. The e-file is half-open and the black king is still on e8.

20.hint: A bishop that watches e7 and f8.
20.why: Ba3 pins the knight on e7 and covers f8. The king is stuck in the middle for good.

32.hint: A knight check that forces a pawn to move.
32.why: Nf6+! gxf6 opens the g-file and the e-file at once, and exf6 shuts the knight on e7 in.

36.prompt: Black threatens Qxf3 and mate on g2. Anderssen ignores it. What does he play?
36.hint: Bring the last rook. Count the checks you will have.
36.why: Rad1!! The famous quiet move. White lets Black take the knight because every White piece is now aimed at the king, and the checks come first.

38.prompt: Start the checks. Give a rook.
38.hint: The knight on e7 is the king's bodyguard.
38.why: Rxe7+! Deflects the knight that guards d7 and opens the e-file.

40.hint: Drag the king onto a square where a double check is coming.
40.why: Qxd7+!! Kxd7 and the king stands on d7 in front of two bishops.

42.hint: Move the bishop with check so the rook checks too.
42.why: Bf5+ is double check from bishop and rook. The king must move, and it has two squares, both losing.

notes.6: The Evans Gambit: a pawn for time and lines.
notes.30: Bxd3 wins back a pawn and points at h7.
notes.44: Bd7+ and the king is driven onto f8.

replays.finale: Two pawns, a knight, a rook and the queen, each one bought a line or a check.

replays.title: Tal and the poisoned pawn
replays.story: Black grabs a pawn on b2 and goes shopping with the queen. Tal lets him. Every move Black spends with the queen is a move Tal spends bringing a piece to the king.

10.prompt: Black's queen attacks b2. Defend it, or offer it?
10.hint: A pawn far from the king is bait. Develop instead.
10.why: Qd2 leaves b2 hanging. If the queen takes, she is three moves from home and White gets those three moves.

14.prompt: Develop with a threat on the queen.
14.hint: The bishop goes to the diagonal of f7 and hits the queen's square.
14.why: Bc4 develops, attacks the queen on a3's escape squares and already looks at f7. Tempo.

16.why: O-O. Black has made four queen moves and developed one bishop. Count the pieces in play.

18.prompt: Bring a rook to the centre.
18.hint: The e-file points at the king.
18.why: Rfe1. The black king is still in the middle; the e-file is where the rook belongs.

24.prompt: Tal's move. The queen goes somewhere amazing.
24.hint: Into the heart of Black's position, offering a knight.
24.why: Qd6!! The queen on d6 stops the king from castling and sits next to it. The knight on c3 hangs: Tal does not care, because taking it costs Black another move.

26.prompt: Black took the knight. Ignore it and bring the rook.
26.hint: The queen on c3 is far from the fight.
26.why: Red1. White has queen and two rooks on the central files; Black's queen is on c3 doing nothing. Every piece counts, but only the ones near the king.

28.why: Bxf7+! Kxf7 drags the king out, and Ng5+ comes with tempo.

30.why: Ng5+ forces the king back to e8, and now Qe6+ is crushing: Qe6+ Kd8 Nf7 mate.

notes.12: Rb1 kicks the queen again: another free move.
notes.32: Qe6+ and Black resigned: Kd8 Nf7 is mate. Black's queen never came home.

replays.finale: Tal gave a pawn and a knight. Black's queen took both and lost the game: tempo beats material.

replays.title: Tal leaves a bishop hanging
replays.story: Against a former world champion, Tal castles on the opposite side, jumps a knight into d6, and leaves a whole bishop hanging for two moves because every move of his makes a threat.

16.prompt: Castle. Which side puts a rook on the open file?
16.why: O-O-O. The rook lands on d1 behind the queen on d4, and White's kingside pawns are free to charge.

18.prompt: Jump a knight into Black's camp.
18.hint: A square the pawns cannot reach, next to the king's defenders.
18.why: Nd6 attacks f7 and b7 and cramps the whole position. A knight on d6 is worth a rook.

20.why: Bc4 points at f7, which only the king defends.

24.prompt: Black attacks the bishop with the queen on a6 and threatens to take it. Tal leaves it. What does he play?
24.hint: Bring the knight to the king's side.
24.why: Nf5! The bishop is bait. Taking it costs Black a move, and Tal uses that move to bring the knight next to the king.

26.prompt: Still leave the bishop. Bring the queen.
26.why: Qh4 threatens Qxh7 ideas with the knight on f5 and bishop on g5. Black finally takes the bishop, but it has cost two moves.

28.hint: Queen next to the king with a threat on g7.
28.why: Qg5 threatens Qxg7 mate. Black must give something.

30.why: Nh6+ forces the king into the corner. Now the h-file and g7 are weak.

36.hint: Qxf7! Count: Rxf7 Nxf7+ forks king and rook.
36.why: Qxf7! If Rxf7 then Nxf7+ wins the rook back with check and White is ahead. Calculated, not hoped.

notes.22: Bd2 steps back and keeps the knight on d6 protected; the c4 bishop is left hanging on purpose.
notes.32: Qxh5 wins back the piece with the attack still running.
notes.38: Qa1+ is a last check. Tal walks away from it.
notes.50: Bd4 and Smyslov resigned. Tal is a pawn up with the better position after a storm of sacrifices.
